paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: Suppose the university newspaper is inviting submissions from the students for its coming edition on the recent developments in their hometown. You are now to write an essay for submission. You will have 30 minutes to write the essay. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：假设大学报纸正在邀请学生为其即将出版的有关家乡最新发展的报纸投稿。您现在需要写一篇论文以供提交。你将有 30 分钟的时间来写这篇文章。您应该写至少 120 个字但不超过 180 个字。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you will hear three news reports. At the end of each news report, you will hear two or three questions. Both the news report and the questions will be spoken only once. After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A), B), C) and D). Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明： 在本节中，您将听到三则新闻报道。在每篇新闻报道的最后，你都会听到两到三个问题。新闻报道和提问均只发言一次。听到问题后，您必须从标有 A)、B)、C) 和 D) 的四个选项中选择最佳答案。然后在答卷 1 上用一条穿过中心的线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 1 and 2 are based on the news report you have just heard.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题1和2是根据你刚才听到的新闻报道得出的。

Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once. After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A), B), C) and D). Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1 with a single line through the centre.

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the passage you have just heard.

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，有一段有十个空格。您需要从文章后面的单词库中给出的选项列表中为每个空白选择一个单词。在做出选择之前仔细阅读该段落。银行中的每个选择都由一个字母标识。请在答题卡 2 上的每个项目上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。您不得多次使用银行中的任何单词。

paragraphs.sourceText: A number of studies have looked at how family life can affect productivity and satisfaction in the workplace. However, there has been 26 little research on the influence of leisure activities. So Ciara Kelly and colleagues recruited 129 hobbyists to look at how the time spent on their hobbies 27 their work life.
paragraphs.translationZh: 许多研究探讨了家庭生活如何影响工作场所的生产力和满意度。然而，令人惊讶的是，关于休闲活动的影响的研究却很少。因此，Ciara Kelly 和同事招募了 129 名业余爱好者来研究他们花在业余爱好上的时间如何影响他们的工作生活。

paragraphs.sourceText: The researchers found that when participants spent longer than 28 on their leisure activity, their belief in their ability to perform their job was strengthened. But this was only the 29 when they had a serious hobby that was dissimilar to their job, or when their hobby was similar to their work but they only did it 30 . When their hobby was both serious and similar to their job, then spending more time on it actually decreased their work 31 .
paragraphs.translationZh: 研究人员发现，当参与者在休闲活动上花费的时间比平时更长时，他们对自己完成工作能力的信心就会增强。但只有当他们有一个与工作不同的严肃爱好时，或者当他们的爱好与工作相似但只是随意做时，才会出现这种情况。当自己的爱好既严肃又与工作相似的时候，花更多的时间在上面，其实反而降低了工作效率。

paragraphs.sourceText: Why might that be? To maintain a serious hobby, people need to invest significant psychological resources, say the authors — so if the activity has the same kinds of demands as their work, they may be left 32 and unable to perform well at their job. But if their hobby is quite different from their career, it may not 33 in the same way but instead help them develop other knowledge and skills that can 34 their confidence at work. “Consider a scientist who is a keen rock climber,” says Kelly. “Since climbing is so far
paragraphs.translationZh: 为什么会这样？作者说，为了保持一种严肃的爱好，人们需要投入大量的心理资源——因此，如果这项活动与他们的工作有同样的要求，他们可能会精疲力尽，无法在工作中表现出色。但如果他们的爱好与他们的职业有很大不同，它可能不会以同样的方式干扰，而是帮助他们发展其他知识和技能，从而增强他们的工作信心。 “想象一下一位热衷于攀岩的科学家，”凯利说。 “既然爬山这么远

paragraphs.sourceText: 35 from their day-to-day work activities, they can still recover from the demands of their job with plenty of resources.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 尽管他们脱离了日常工作活动，但仍然可以利用充足的资源从工作需求中恢复过来。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: More fathers are taking paternity leave, but mothers are still doing all the work
paragraphs.translationZh: 越来越多的父亲正在休陪产假，但母亲仍在承担所有工作

paragraphs.sourceText: A) Attitudes towards paternity leave (陪产假) have drastically changed in America in the last five years as more fathers feel comfortable taking extended time off, but gender bias persists when it comes to career prospects and the home, according to a new study of working parents.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 一项针对在职父母的最新研究显示，过去五年来，随着越来越多的父亲愿意延长休假时间，美国对陪产假的态度发生了巨大变化，但在职业前景和家庭方面，性别偏见依然存在。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) Research by the Boston College Center for Work & Family, which surveyed new parents at four large U.S. companies who were qualified for taking at least six weeks paid parental leave, found that 81% of the 1,240 employees surveyed said the notion of fathers taking leave has become more acceptable.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 波士顿学院工作与家庭中心对美国四家大公司的新晋父母进行了一项调查，这些公司有资格享受至少六周带薪育儿假，结果发现，在接受调查的 1,240 名员工中，81% 的人表示，父亲休假的概念已经变得更容易被接受。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) Of those surveyed, 62% of fathers took the maximum amount of time off compared to 93% of mothers, and around three-quarters of workers said their employer was equally supportive of mothers and fathers taking parental leave and over half said leave policies had made workplace culture better.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 在受访者中，62% 的父亲休了最长的休假时间，而母亲的这一比例为 93%，大约四分之三的员工表示，他们的雇主同样支持母亲和父亲休育儿假，超过一半的人表示，休假政策改善了工作场所文化。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) The U.S. is one of only three countries in the world not to offer statutory (法定的) paid leave, but increasingly states and companies are starting to take up the issue. So far, eight states and the District of Columbia have their own paid family leave laws.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 美国是世界上仅有的三个不提供法定带薪休假的国家之一，但越来越多的州和公司开始关注这个问题。到目前为止，八个州和哥伦比亚特区都有自己的带薪家庭假法。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) Brad Harrington, executive director of the center and lead author of the study, estimates only 20% to 30% of companies in the U.S. offer paid parental leave. He feels the research findings reflect an obvious change in corporate attitudes to new fathers taking time off.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 该中心的执行董事兼该研究的主要作者 Brad Harrington 估计，美国只有 20% 到 30% 的公司提供带薪育儿假。他认为研究结果反映出企业对新爸爸休假的态度发生了明显变化。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) “We did a study on paternity leave five years ago. Compared with those findings, these numbers were shocking to me. I did not expect 80% of people to say the organisation finds dads taking this leave acceptable and three-quarters to say it’s equally supportive of women and men taking leave,” Harrington said.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) “五年前，我们对陪产假进行了一项研究。与这些研究结果相比，这些数字令我震惊。我没想到，80% 的人表示，该组织认为父亲休陪产假是可以接受的，四分之三的人表示，该组织同样支持女性和男性休陪产假，”哈林顿说。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) The previous study found that nearly three-quarters of fathers saw two to four weeks as an appropriate duration for paternity leave and 76% said they would prefer not to take all their time off at once.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 之前的研究发现，近四分之三的父亲认为两到四个星期的陪产假比较合适，76% 的父亲表示他们不愿意立即休掉所有的时间。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) Since then, there have been a number of legal cases against companies involving paternity leave — including cases against JPMorgan Chase and Estée Lauder — which have helped put pressure on companies to make their parental leave policies gender neutral.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 从那时起，出现了许多针对涉及陪产假的公司的法律案件——包括针对摩根大通和雅诗兰黛的案件——这有助于向公司施加压力，要求其制定产假政策中性别中立。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) However, the study also shows how traditional gender roles endure both at work, where more women than men reported changes in their perceived career potential, and at home — even among workers who claim to have a strong desire for equality.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 然而，该研究还表明，传统的性别角色在工作中和家庭中都持续存在，在工作中，女性比男性更多地报告了她们所感知的职业潜力的变化，甚至在那些声称强烈渴望平等的工人中也是如此。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) The vast majority of men, 97%, said one of the top reasons to take leave was to share caregiving with their partner. But when they were asked about how caregiving and household tasks were divided, their answers painted a different picture. While about 75% of employees said both genders should give the same amount of care, the majority of men and nearly half of women admitted that in reality the female actually did most of it. A tiny fraction, 2%, of men said they did more of the childcare.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 绝大多数男性（97%）表示请假的首要原因之一是与伴侣分担照顾。但当他们被问及如何划分看护和家务任务时，他们的答案却描绘了不同的景象。虽然大约 75% 的员工表示男女应该给予同等程度的照顾，但大多数男性和近一半女性承认，实际上大部分工作都是女性承担的。一小部分（2%）的男性表示，他们承担了更多的育儿工作。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) Men and women’s experiences of the return to work following parental leave were also considerably different. Of the women surveyed, 32% reported a downturn in their job satisfaction, while 14% said it increased. In comparison, 17% of men said their job satisfaction went down and 20% said it went up. Meanwhile, more women reported an increase in their responsibilities and manager expectations after childbirth. Half of the women said they used flexible work arrangements after becoming a parent, while just 27% of men did. Similar percentages of men and women said they enjoyed their careers and that it gave them a sense of achievement, while around half of women and 44% of men said it was a key part of their identity.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 男性和女性在育儿假后重返工作岗位的经历也有很大不同。在接受调查的女性中，32% 的女性表示她们的工作满意度下降，而 14% 的女性则表示工作满意度有所上升。相比之下，17% 的男性表示他们的工作满意度下降，20% 的男性表示工作满意度上升。与此同时，更多的女性表示，产后她们的责任和管理者的期望有所增加。一半的女性表示，她们在成为父母后采用了灵活的工作安排，而只有 27% 的男性表示这样做。相似比例的男性和女性表示，他们喜欢自己的职业生涯，这给了他们成就感，而大约一半的女性和 44% 的男性则表示，这是他们身份的重要组成部分。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) On the subject of career advancement, 59% of women and 49% of men said leave could be limiting and both genders said they feared it would have an impact on their progress long-term. But on opportunity for promotion, more than double the number of women, 30% compared with 15% of men, believed their chances to be lower after becoming a parent. Despite progress, the struggle for women to reach the highest positions of power is demonstrated in this year’s Fortune 500 list, which featured a record 33 female CEOs, but this still represents a tiny fraction of the total.
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 在职业发展方面，59% 的女性和 49% 的男性表示休假可能会受到限制，而且男女都表示他们担心这会对他们的长期进步产生影响。但在晋升机会方面，认为成为父母后晋升机会会降低的女性人数（30% 和 15%）是男性的两倍多。尽管取得了进步，但今年的《财富》500 强榜单显示了女性为获得最高权力职位而进行的斗争，其中女性首席执行官人数达到创纪录的 33 名，但这仍然只占总数的一小部分。

paragraphs.sourceText: M) Harrington said culture change depends on companies putting more focus on men and their responsibilities. “By that I mean companies need to give men paternity leave and encourage men to take time off to be with their kids early on in the kids’ life. They also need to recognise that men have to make significant adjustments when they become parents. Companies cannot do all these things to enhance women’s advancement and then turn around and say, ‘Oh, but we don’t expect the men to take over for the women at home.’ ”
paragraphs.translationZh: M) Harrington 表示，文化变革取决于公司更加关注男性及其责任。 “我的意思是，公司需要给予男性陪产假，并鼓励男性在孩子还小的时候就抽出时间陪伴孩子。他们还需要认识到，男性在成为父母后必须做出重大调整。公司不能做所有这些事情来提高女性的进步，然后转身说，‘哦，但我们不希望男性接管女性的家庭。’”

paragraphs.sourceText: N) In May, the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) and Outten & Golden LLP announced a historic class-action $5m settlement with JPMorgan Chase on behalf of male employees who claim they were illegally denied access to paid parental leave. Derek Rotondo, 35, filed the discrimination charge against his company after he was allegedly told by his HR department that mothers were considered primary caregivers. Thus, they were allowed to take 16 weeks of paid parental leave. Fathers, however, could take just two weeks.
paragraphs.translationZh: N) 5 月，美国公民自由联盟 (ACLU) 和 Outten & Golden LLP 代表那些声称自己被非法剥夺带薪育儿假的男性员工，宣布与摩根大通达成历史性的 500 万美元集体诉讼和解。 35 岁的德里克·罗通多 (Derek Rotondo) 据称在人力资源部门告诉他母亲被视为主要照顾者后，对他的公司提出了歧视指控。因此，他们可以享受 16 周的带薪育儿假。然而，父亲们可能只需要两周的时间。

paragraphs.sourceText: O) The father of two from Columbus, Ohio, who still works at the company as an associate and investigator, said he has witnessed a “domino effect (多米诺效应)” across companies since the settlement, but that there is still substantial progress to be made towards changing attitudes towards paternity leave.
paragraphs.translationZh: 来自俄亥俄州哥伦布市的 O) 是两个孩子的父亲，目前仍在该公司担任助理和调查员。他表示，自和解以来，他亲眼目睹了各公司之间的“多米诺效应”，但在改变对陪产假的态度方面仍需取得实质性进展。

paragraphs.sourceText: P. “I do think there’s still some way to go...there’s still going to be sort of the unstated expectation for new dads to essentially come right back to work, but I think the research is showing that’s starting to change.” He said equal parental leave is an essential component to creating gender equality in the workplace. “The old standard of women staying home, having babies and cooking doesn’t apply and hasn’t applied for a long time.”
paragraphs.translationZh: P.“我确实认为还有很长的路要走……对于新爸爸们基本上会立即重返工作岗位仍然存在某种未明确的期望，但我认为研究表明这种情况正在开始改变。”他说，平等育儿假是在工作场所实现性别平等的重要组成部分。 “女性待在家里、生孩子和做饭的旧标准不再适用，而且已经很长时间不适用了。”

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. In the absence of Federal legislation, some states in the U.S. have passed laws concerning paid family leave.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 在缺乏联邦立法的情况下，美国的一些州通过了有关带薪家庭假的法律。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. Most fathers admitted that even during their paternity leave they actually did much less childcare than the
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 大多数父亲承认，即使在休陪产假期间，他们照顾孩子的时间实际上也比父母少得多。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. According to one father, equal parental leave is indispensable to achieving gender equality in the workplace.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 一位父亲表示，平等育儿假对于实现工作场所性别平等必不可少。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. One survey indicated there is now less objection to paternity leave.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 一项调查表明，现在对陪产假的反对较少。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. Compared to five years ago, according to one researcher, many more people said their organisation gave the same support to men and women taking parental leave.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 一位研究人员表示，与五年前相比，更多的人表示他们的组织对休育儿假的男性和女性提供了同样的支持。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. One study finds that even workers who claim to desire gender equality stick to traditional gender roles both at work and at home.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 一项研究发现，即使是声称渴望性别平等的工人，在工作和家庭中也坚持传统的性别角色。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. The majority of workers surveyed said parental leave policies had improved workplace culture.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 大多数接受调查的工人表示，育儿假政策改善了工作场所文化。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. In spite of progress, the number of women in top positions of big companies remains extremely small.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 尽管取得了进展，但担任大公司高层职位的妇女人数仍然极少。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. According to one estimate, less than one third of companies in the U.S. provide paid parental leave.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 据一项估计，美国只有不到三分之一的公司提供带薪育儿假。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. A number of lawsuits have pressured companies to formulate gender neutral policies on parental leave.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 许多诉讼迫使公司制定性别中立的育儿假政策。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：本节有 2 段。每段文章后面都有一些问题或未完成的陈述。每个选项都有四个选项，标记为 A)、B)、C) 和 D)。您应该决定最佳选择，并在答题卡 2 上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Having a rival can keep you committed to achieving your goals and enhance your overall performance. But before you go out and find an entrepreneur to outcompete, it’s important to understand and avoid the traps that often come with rivalry. After all, competitive rivalry can also hinder effective decision-making and increase your willingness to take risks, behaviors that can ultimately hurt your venture’s success.
paragraphs.translationZh: 拥有竞争对手可以让您致力于实现目标并提高您的整体表现。但在你出去寻找一位能够在竞争中获胜的企业家之前，了解并避免竞争中经常出现的陷阱非常重要。毕竟，竞争也会阻碍有效的决策并增加你冒险的意愿，而这些行为最终可能会损害你企业的成功。

paragraphs.sourceText: Finding someone you’re committed to outcompeting can be a great way to stay focused on your goals and push your venture to the next level. But when you’re intently focused on outperforming your rivals, you may begin to develop a “win-at-all-costs” mentality that causes you to ignore how you achieve success. One group of researchers, for example, examined the link between rivalry and unethical behavior. They found that when people compete against their rivals, they are more willing to behave unethically to win. But such behavior may stain your reputation and strain relationships important to your success. One way to avoid this trap is to stop and reflect on what’s important. While outperforming your rivals may provide short-term benefits, the loss of your integrity will have long-term consequences.
paragraphs.translationZh: 找到一个你致力于在竞争中胜出的人是一个很好的方法，可以让你专注于你的目标，并将你的企业推向新的水平。但当你全神贯注于超越竞争对手时，你可能会开始养成一种“不惜一切代价取胜”的心态，导致你忽视如何取得成功。例如，一组研究人员研究了竞争与不道德行为之间的联系。他们发现，当人们与对手竞争时，他们更愿意做出不道德的行为来赢得胜利。但这种行为可能会损害你的声誉，并使对你的成功至关重要的人际关系紧张。避免这个陷阱的一种方法是停下来反思什么是重要的。虽然超越竞争对手可能会带来短期利益，但诚信的丧失将带来长期后果。

paragraphs.sourceText: One reason having a rival can enhance your venture’s performance is that it creates a level of excitement that drives you to work harder. But this eagerness to win may also hurt your venture’s success, particularly when it causes you to make impulsive, insensible decisions. But it’s possible to avoid such costly mistakes by making a habit of engaging in critical thinking, such as considering opposing viewpoints and conducting cost-benefit analyses, especially for those decisions that are complex and can determine the future of your venture.
paragraphs.translationZh: 拥有竞争对手可以提高你的企业绩效的一个原因是，它会产生一定程度的兴奋感，促使你更加努力地工作。但这种对胜利的渴望也可能会损害你企业的成功，尤其是当它导致你做出冲动、不明智的决定时。但是，可以通过养成批判性思维的习惯来避免这种代价高昂的错误，例如考虑相反的观点和进行成本效益分析，特别是对于那些复杂且可以决定企业未来的决策。

paragraphs.sourceText: The sense of eagerness that comes with having a rival can not only cause you to make poorer decisions, but it can also lead you to take greater risks that put your venture in peril. One way you can overcome the risk-inducing effects of rivalry that stand to endanger your venture’s success is to remain attentive to your emotional state and actively monitor how such feelings are affecting your decision-making.
paragraphs.translationZh: 拥有竞争对手所带来的急切感不仅会导致你做出糟糕的决定，还会导致你承担更大的风险，从而使你的企业陷入危险。克服可能危及企业成功的竞争带来的风险影响的一种方法是，持续关注自己的情绪状态，并积极监测这些情绪如何影响您的决策。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: A multitasker is one who can perform two or more tasks effectively at the same time, which — apart from the obvious differences — is similar to what a computer does. The concept does indeed come from the realms of technology, where it is used to refer to an operating system that can execute multiple tasks at the same time. However, the question is: can a person really be a multitasker?
paragraphs.translationZh: 多任务处理者是指能够同时有效地执行两项或多项任务的人，除了明显的差异外，这与计算机的工作类似。这个概念确实来自技术领域，它用来指可以同时执行多个任务的操作系统。然而，问题是：一个人真的可以同时处理多项任务吗？

paragraphs.sourceText: For most scientists, the answer is no. So much so that, according to experts in neuroscience(神经系统科学), our brains do not handle multitasking situations well. As soon as two tasks require our attention, productivity suffers. What we call multitasking, therefore, is in reality the ability to move more or less quickly from one task to another. This requires two essential conditions: that one of the tasks needs to be automatic, like walking or eating, and that they both need different mental processes. Answering the phone and writing at the same time, for example.
paragraphs.translationZh: 对于大多数科学家来说，答案是否定的。根据神经系统科学专家的说法，我们的大脑不能很好地处理多任务情况。一旦有两项任务需要我们集中注意力，生产力就会受到影响。因此，我们所说的多任务实际上是或多或少快速地从​​一项任务转移到另一项任务的能力。这需要两个基本条件：其中一项任务需要是自动的，例如走路或吃饭，并且它们都需要不同的心理过程。例如，同时接电话和写信。

paragraphs.sourceText: However, on the other side of the coin there are people who maintain that it is possible to be, or at least seem to be, multitasking. A recent study concluded that regardless of whether people are actually handling several tasks or not, the mere fact that they perceive this activity as multitasking has a positive effect on their performance.
paragraphs.translationZh: 然而，另一方面，也有人坚持认为，或者至少看起来是可以同时处理多项任务。最近的一项研究得出的结论是，无论人们是否实际上正在处理多项任务，只要他们将这项活动视为多任务处理，这一事实就会对其表现产生积极影响。

paragraphs.sourceText: The business perspective offers a different view: multitasking is understood as the ability to adapt to all types of environment within a company and effectively undertake different activities within a set time frame. Indeed, many companies look for people who are skilled in multitasking to improve their productivity. From this different perspective, you can not only be multitasking but this ability can also be taught: something that is easier in fluid organisations, which favour flexibility in their working practices.
paragraphs.translationZh: 商业角度提供了不同的观点：多任务处理被理解为适应公司内各种类型的环境并在设定的时间范围内有效地开展不同活动的能力。事实上，许多公司都在寻找能够同时处理多项任务的人来提高他们的生产力。从这个不同的角度来看，你不仅可以同时处理多项任务，而且这种能力也可以被教授：在流动组织中更容易做到这一点，因为流动组织有利于工作实践的灵活性。

paragraphs.sourceText: The benefits of multitasking are clear. Being quicker and more efficient increases our performance and the number of tasks completed. But having to pay attention to several things at once means that the powers of concentration are reduced and that can lead to more mistakes.
paragraphs.translationZh: 多任务处理的好处是显而易见的。更快、更高效可以提高我们的绩效和完成的任务数量。但必须同时注意几件事情意味着注意力会减弱，从而可能导致更多错误。
